Usage

Smooths an ordered sequence of 3D points with a B-spline and resamples it. → (M,3). For smoothing noisy trajectories/edges.

scipy.interpolate.splprep/splev. smooth=0 interpolates, >0 smooths. n = number of output points (default = number of inputs).

Fits a parametric B-spline with splprep([x, y, z], s=smooth, k=k) (parameter u∈[0,1], scipy's default chord-length parameterisation), evaluates it with splev at u = linspace(0, 1, n), and returns (n,3) float64. Since u is evenly spaced, the output points are not strictly evenly spaced in arc length (if you need even arc-length spacing, pass the result through resample_uniform).

• smooth: scipy's smoothing condition s. Fits with the fewest knots such that the residual sum of squares is at most s. 0 gives an interpolation through all points; the larger, the smoother (units are coordinates squared).

• k: spline degree (default 3). ValueError if the number of points N is k or less.

• n: number of output points. None means the number of input points.

• The input is assumed to be (N,3) ordered by index; there is no shape check other than the number of points.

Used as a pre-stage to smooth noisy edge point sequences or trajectories before passing them to curvature_torsion / frenet_frame. To carry tck around, use fit_bspline_curve / eval_bspline_curve.

The 3d op fit_spline_curve bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). a sweeps k (default 3). b is unused.
